questions.explanation: Cardiovascular disease is a major cause of excess mortality in longstanding RA.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: Patient came with hemorrhagic shock, what is the first priority in management?
questions.explanation: In hemorrhagic shock, the priority is control of the source of bleeding while simultaneously initiating resuscitation. Definitive hemorrhage control is critical to prevent ongoing blood loss.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A 42 year-old female patient known having Rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate weekly what drug should be used with it:
questions.explanation: Methotrexate inhibits folate metabolism and can cause mucositis, cytopenias and hepatotoxicity. Folic acid supplementation reduces adverse effects while maintaining therapeutic efficacy.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A patient in hospital with MRSA cellulitis the best antibiotic to be initiated for the treatment is:
questions.explanation: MRSA is resistant to standard anti-staphylococcal β-lactams such as flucloxacillin. Vancomycin is a standard treatment for serious hospitalized MRSA infection.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A woman taking oral contraceptive, which drug will interact with it:
questions.explanation: Rifampicin is a potent hepatic enzyme inducer and increases metabolism of estrogen/progestogen, reducing the effectiveness of combined hormonal contraceptives.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A Female patient with pneumonia was injected with amoxicillin, then she developed dyspnea, hypotension and itching, what's the type of hypersensitivity responsible for this reaction?
questions.explanation: Dyspnea, hypotension and itching immediately after a β-lactam strongly indicate anaphylaxis, which is a Type I IgE-mediated immediate hypersensitivity reaction.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: Patient had trauma and on abdominal examination, he had Cullen's sign, what is the cause here?
questions.explanation: Cullen's sign is periumbilical ecchymosis caused by intra-abdominal or retroperitoneal bleeding. In a trauma patient, intra-abdominal hemorrhage is an important cause.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A Female patient came to you with malaise, having fissures on the angles of her lips, on examination she had a painless mass in the right iliac fossa with unknown cause, what is the cause here?
questions.explanation: Angular cheilitis can occur with iron deficiency. Iron deficiency may also cause fatigue, pallor, glossitis and other mucocutaneous manifestations.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: Which of the following causing mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis?
questions.explanation: Leishmania braziliensis is classically associated with mucocutaneous leishmaniasis, particularly in South America.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: Parkinson disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative condition, which is the neurotransmitter is responsible for this disease?
questions.explanation: Parkinson disease is associated with degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra, resulting in reduced dopamine in the striatum.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A GP got needle stick of patient who was an IV drug abuser, having infective endocarditis, what is the probable causative organism here?
questions.explanation: S. aureus is the most common cause of infective endocarditis in intravenous drug users.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: What is the most common cause of Hospital-acquired pneumonia?
questions.explanation: Among the options given, Staphylococcus aureus is the best answer. Hospital-acquired pneumonia is commonly caused by aerobic Gram-negative bacilli and S. aureus.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: Which of the following drug is contraindicated in psoriasisis:
questions.explanation: Systemic corticosteroids are generally avoided in psoriasis because withdrawal can precipitate severe rebound psoriasis, including generalized pustular psoriasis. Methotrexate, cyclosporine and acitretin are all established psoriasis treatments.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A pregnant female patient complaining of sudden onset abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding ,she is in 38 weeks ,her BP110/80 and there is lower abdominal tenderness ,her baby pulse rate 170bpm, the most important diagnosis:
questions.explanation: Placental abruption typically presents with painful vaginal bleeding, abdominal/uterine tenderness and fetal distress. Placenta previa classically causes painless bleeding.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: Consultant wanted to find evidence about incidence of deep venous thrombosis, the most accurate study is:
questions.explanation: Incidence means the occurrence of new cases over time. A cohort study can follow disease-free individuals and measure the incidence of DVT.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A 5 year-old child patient with skin lesion not itchy,painless on his chest, no fever, and systematically well ,which of the following is most appropriate dignosis:
questions.explanation: Molluscum contagiosum produces painless, usually non-itchy, pearly papules with central umbilication. The child is usually systemically well.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A young patient complaining of vomiting and fatigue for few days then has dark urine, the possible cause is:
questions.explanation: Acute viral hepatitis can cause constitutional symptoms followed by jaundice and dark urine due to conjugated bilirubinuria.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: Terry's nails are found in patients with:
questions.explanation: Terry's nails are characterized by whitening of most of the nail with a distal band and are classically associated with chronic liver disease, especially cirrhosis.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: The most serious complication of measles is:
questions.explanation: SSPE is a rare but devastating, progressive neurological complication occurring years after measles infection. It causes progressive cognitive and neurological deterioration and is usually fatal.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A male patient with stabbing pain in jaw and mouth for few seconds which increased during toothbrush, what is the best drug for treatment:
questions.explanation: Brief, severe, electric-shock-like facial pain triggered by touching the face or brushing teeth is characteristic of trigeminal neuralgia. Carbamazepine is a classic first-line treatment.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A 62 year-old male patient with heart rate 72bpm and BP 220/110 mmHg with radio-femoral delay, audible systolic murmer, and notching in ribs at MCL on chest X.ray what is the possible diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Radio-femoral delay, severe hypertension and rib notching due to collateral circulation are classic findings of coarctation of the aorta.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A Patient with severe central chest pain, which radiates to left shoulder and jaw, he is stable with BP 150/100mmHg and pulse rate 74 bpm, he took aspirin, what is the next drug he should take?
questions.explanation: In the context of the options provided, diamorphine is used for severe persistent pain associated with suspected acute coronary syndrome. Aspirin has already been given.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A 3-year-old child with a history of diarrhea 6 times per day for 6 months, with visible vegetable matter in stools. The child is thriving well, and development is normal. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Toddler's diarrhea is a common cause of chronic loose stools in otherwise healthy children who have normal growth and development. Undigested food particles may be visible in stool.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: An elderly patient with watery diarrhea 6 times a day was admitted to the hospital due to an infection exacerbation while on co-amoxiclav. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Recent antibiotic exposure, particularly broad-spectrum antibiotics such as co-amoxiclav, predisposes to C. difficile infection causing antibiotic-associated watery diarrhea.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A case of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), what is the correct dose of insulin infusion?
questions.explanation: Standard IV insulin infusion for DKA is commonly 0.1 units/kg/hour, with monitoring and adjustment according to glucose, ketones and metabolic response.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A type I diabetic patient is on 15 units of long-acting insulin at night and regular insulin three times at meals. The patient is preparing for an anesthetic operation and fasting from midnight. What should be done regarding insulin?
options: Omit insulin at night and morning
Give insulin at night but not in the morning
questions.explanation: A patient with type 1 diabetes must not be left completely without insulin because of the risk of DKA. During surgery/fasting, insulin requirements need adjustment and often a variable-rate IV insulin regimen with glucose monitoring is used.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: An adult wanted to start a family and he has Hemorrhagic telangiectasia, what is the type of inheritance?
questions.explanation: HHT is usually inherited as an autosomal dominant disorder. Variable expression and incomplete penetrance can occur.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A grandfather is a carrier of cystic fibrosis. What is the risk for his grandson who is 5 year- old?
questions.explanation: Assuming the grandfather is a carrier and the child's parent is his child, the carrier probability for that parent is 1/2. If the other parent is assumed not to be a carrier, the probability of passing the CF allele to the grandson is 1/4 if considering only transmission from a carrier parent. However, the exact pedigree is incompletely specified; 1:8 is the intended exam answer in the supplied model.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A patient with hypertension and radio-femoral delay, with rib notching seen on X-ray at the midclavicular line. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The combination of hypertension, radio-femoral delay and rib notching is highly characteristic of coarctation of the aorta.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: Which of the following give the best description to study the new cases of papilloma virus infection in collage student?
questions.explanation: The question asks about new cases. Incidence measures the number/rate of new cases occurring in a defined population during a specified period.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: In a patient with acute cholecystitis, what is the most common radiological imaging for the case?
questions.explanation: Ultrasound is the usual first-line imaging investigation for suspected acute cholecystitis and is particularly useful for detecting gallstones, gallbladder wall thickening and sonographic Murphy sign.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A patient comes to the GP with unilateral painful redness of the eye, with no discharge. What should the doctor do next?
options: Referral to ophthalmology emergency department for assessment
questions.explanation: A painful unilateral red eye without discharge can represent serious ocular disease such as acute glaucoma, keratitis or uveitis. Steroid drops should not be given without appropriate ophthalmological assessment.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A GP doctor got needle stick injury while performing venous cannula to patient known of intravenous drug use, what is the frist thing to do?
options: Encourage bleeding from site needle of the stick injury
questions.explanation: The incident should be immediately reported through the occupational exposure protocol so that risk assessment and appropriate HIV/HBV post-exposure management can be initiated promptly.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: Which of the following antituberculosis drugs requires visual monitoring?
questions.explanation: Ethambutol can cause optic neuritis, resulting in reduced visual acuity and red-green color discrimination abnormalities. Baseline and appropriate follow-up visual assessment is therefore important.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: What is the best test for diagnosing giant cell arteritis?
questions.explanation: Temporal artery biopsy is the classic confirmatory diagnostic test for giant cell arteritis. Treatment with corticosteroids should not be unnecessarily delayed when clinical suspicion is high.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A patient presents with finger deformity after trauma with inability to extend his finger. What should be done for the deformity?
questions.explanation: Inability to actively extend the distal interphalangeal joint after trauma suggests a mallet finger. Most uncomplicated cases are treated initially with continuous extension splinting.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: Most conforming test for Pernicious anemia is:
questions.explanation: Pernicious anemia causes vitamin B12 deficiency due to autoimmune destruction of gastric parietal cells and intrinsic-factor deficiency. Serum B12 demonstrates the deficiency, although anti-intrinsic-factor antibodies can help establish the specific cause.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: An old patient presents with gum bleeding and hypertrophy. Which nutritional deficiency could be the cause?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C deficiency causes defective collagen synthesis, leading to fragile capillaries, bleeding gums, gingival swelling and poor wound healing.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A mother with deafness from age 12 and using a hearing aid wants to confirm if her new baby is deaf. Which test should be used?
questions.explanation: Auditory brainstem response (ABR/BAER) is an objective test used for hearing assessment in newborns, especially when behavioral hearing testing is not possible.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A patient had a carotid artery surgery, the he has difficulty speaking, and when protruding the tongue, it deviates toward the right side. Which nerve is affected?
questions.explanation: The hypoglossal nerve supplies the tongue muscles. With a unilateral lower motor neuron lesion, the protruded tongue deviates toward the side of the lesion.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A patient complains of dysphagia and is diagnosed with middle esophageal cancer that has metastasized to the liver. What is the best method to improve dysphagia in this patient?
questions.explanation: In advanced esophageal cancer with metastatic disease, an esophageal stent can provide rapid palliation of dysphagia and improve oral intake.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A patient with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and lupus nephritis, Which marker indicates activity of lupus nephritis?
questions.explanation: Anti-double-stranded DNA antibodies correlate with SLE disease activity, particularly renal disease, and rising levels can be associated with lupus nephritis activity.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A girl had a sore throat with slight fever, malaise, then she developed maculopapular and partially vesicular spots on the hands and feet, with oral ulcers, what's the most likely cause:
questions.explanation: Hand-foot-and-mouth disease is classically caused by enteroviruses, especially Coxsackie A viruses. It causes oral ulcers and vesicular lesions on the hands and feet.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A 62 year-old male patient with low immunity came with productive cough and dyspnea and CXR is showing chest infection, the indication of sputum examination is for:
questions.explanation: In an immunocompromised patient with respiratory symptoms, particularly when TB is clinically suspected, sputum examination is important for detecting Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A 22 year- old male patient complaining of swelling in left testis, can't be separated from the testis ,the it is firm and fluctuating, with bright trans illumination ,which of the following is true :
questions.explanation: A hydrocele is a fluid collection around the testis and classically transilluminates. The description of bright transillumination strongly supports hydrocele.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: Which is MOST SINGLE investigation aid in diagnosis of hepatocellular carcenoma:
questions.explanation: Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is a commonly used tumor marker in hepatocellular carcinoma. It is not sufficiently sensitive or specific to be used alone for diagnosis, but among the listed options it is clearly the best answer.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: Patient came with urticaria, what's the most dangerous type?
questions.explanation: Angioedema involving the tongue, pharynx or larynx can cause life-threatening airway obstruction.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: A 3 year-old girl patient in pediatrics department suffering from lower UTI, then the pediatrician ordered for her septrin about 2mg/kg, and her weight is about 12.5 kg, what is the required amount in ml of septrin "50mg/5ml" she will take every night?
questions.explanation: Dose = 2 mg/kg × 12.5 kg = 25 mg. Concentration = 50 mg/5 mL = 10 mg/mL. Volume = 25 mg ÷ 10 mg/mL = 2.5 mL.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: Which is of the following about acute respiratory distress syndrome is correct?
questions.explanation: ARDS causes severe impairment of oxygenation, resulting in a reduced PaO2/FiO2 ratio.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: Which of the following may be present in patient with hyperthyrodism:
questions.explanation: Pretibial myxedema is an extrathyroidal manifestation of Graves disease and may occur in patients with hyperthyroidism.

questions.subject: medical
questions.text: The best initial test to do in patient with Tinea infestation:
questions.explanation: KOH preparation of a skin scraping is a simple initial investigation for suspected dermatophyte infection and can demonstrate fungal hyphae.

questions.subject: Rheumatology
questions.text: A 42-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis is taking weekly methotrexate. Which supplement should routinely be given with methotrexate?
questions.explanation: Folic acid is routinely supplemented with low-dose methotrexate to reduce folate-related adverse effects such as mucositis and cytopenias without substantially reducing efficacy.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Infectious Diseases
questions.text: A hospitalized patient has MRSA cellulitis. Which antibiotic is the best treatment?
questions.explanation: Vancomycin is a standard intravenous treatment for serious MRSA skin and soft-tissue infection in hospitalized patients.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Immunology
questions.text: A woman with pneumonia receives amoxicillin and then develops dyspnea, hypotension, and itching. What type of hypersensitivity reaction is responsible?
questions.explanation: Dyspnea, hypotension, and itching occurring rapidly after amoxicillin are characteristic of anaphylaxis, a type I IgE-mediated immediate hypersensitivity reaction.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Gastroenterology
questions.text: A woman has malaise and fissures at the angles of her lips. Examination reveals a painless right iliac fossa mass. Which condition or deficiency best explains the presentation?
questions.explanation: The source option appears to refer to Crohn disease/Crohn-related nutritional deficiency. A painless right iliac fossa mass with malaise can occur in Crohn disease, and nutritional deficiencies may cause angular cheilitis. The option wording is unclear.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Neurology
questions.text: Which neurotransmitter deficiency is most closely associated with Parkinson disease?
questions.explanation: Parkinson disease is associated with degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra and reduced dopamine in the striatum.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Infectious Diseases
questions.text: A general practitioner sustains a needlestick injury from a patient who injects drugs and has infective endocarditis. Which organism is most likely to have caused the endocarditis?
questions.explanation: Staphylococcus aureus is the most common cause of infective endocarditis among people who inject drugs, particularly involving the tricuspid valve.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.text: Which drug is contraindicated or generally avoided in psoriasis because withdrawal may precipitate severe rebound disease?
questions.explanation: Systemic corticosteroids are generally avoided in psoriasis because withdrawal can precipitate severe rebound psoriasis, including generalized pustular psoriasis.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.text: A pregnant woman at 38 weeks has sudden abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding, lower abdominal tenderness, and fetal tachycardia. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Painful vaginal bleeding with uterine/lower abdominal tenderness and fetal tachycardia at term is most consistent with placental abruption. Placenta previa classically causes painless bleeding.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.text: A 5-year-old child has a painless, non-itchy chest skin lesion, no fever, and is otherwise well. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Molluscum contagiosum commonly causes painless, non-itchy umbilicated papules in otherwise well children.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Gastroenterology
questions.text: A young patient has vomiting and fatigue for several days followed by dark urine. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Acute viral hepatitis can cause malaise, vomiting, and dark urine from conjugated hyperbilirubinemia during the icteric phase.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.text: What is the most serious delayed complication of measles?
questions.explanation: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis is a rare, progressive, and ultimately fatal delayed neurologic complication of measles infection.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Neurology
questions.text: A man has brief stabbing facial pain lasting seconds and triggered by toothbrushing. What is the best drug treatment?
questions.explanation: Brief electric-shock-like facial pain triggered by activities such as brushing the teeth is typical of trigeminal neuralgia; carbamazepine is a standard first-line drug.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Cardiology
questions.text: A 62-year-old man has severe hypertension, radio-femoral delay, a systolic murmur, and rib notching on chest X-ray. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Radio-femoral delay, severe hypertension, a systolic murmur, and rib notching are classic findings of coarctation of the aorta.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Emergency Medicine
questions.text: A patient has severe central chest pain radiating to the left shoulder and jaw and has already taken aspirin. What is the next appropriate medication among the options?
questions.explanation: The question appears to refer to older acute coronary syndrome treatment where diamorphine was used for severe pain. Modern ACS care prioritizes urgent ECG/reperfusion assessment and analgesia only when needed; routine opioids are not universally recommended.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.text: A thriving 3-year-old has six loose stools daily for six months with visible vegetable matter in the stool and normal development. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Chronic loose stools with visible food particles in a thriving, normally developing 3-year-old are characteristic of toddler's diarrhea (functional diarrhea).
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Infectious Diseases
questions.text: An elderly hospitalized patient develops frequent watery diarrhea after treatment with co-amoxiclav. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Recent co-amoxiclav exposure followed by significant watery diarrhea in a hospitalized patient strongly suggests Clostridioides difficile infection.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Endocrinology
questions.text: What is the usual initial intravenous insulin infusion rate for diabetic ketoacidosis?
questions.explanation: A commonly used initial intravenous regular insulin infusion rate for DKA is 0.1 unit/kg/hour, with subsequent adjustment according to glucose and metabolic response.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Endocrinology
questions.text: A patient with type 1 diabetes uses basal insulin at night and regular insulin with meals and is fasting for surgery. How should perioperative insulin be managed?
options: Omit insulin at night and morning
Give insulin at night but not in the morning
questions.explanation: A patient with type 1 diabetes must not have basal insulin completely omitted. Perioperative insulin is adjusted with glucose monitoring, often using a variable-rate IV insulin regimen for prolonged fasting or major surgery.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Genetics
questions.text: What is the inheritance pattern of hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia?
questions.explanation: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia is an autosomal dominant disorder with variable expression; incomplete penetrance can occur.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Genetics
questions.text: A grandfather is a carrier of cystic fibrosis. What is the risk that his grandson inherits the familial CF variant, assuming the relevant intervening parent and other parent are unaffected/non-carriers as appropriate?
questions.explanation: The question is incomplete because the carrier status of the intervening parent and the other biological parent is not specified. If the intervening parent has a 1/2 chance of being a carrier and then transmits the variant with a 1/2 chance, the grandson's chance of inheriting one CF variant is 1/4; this is not the same as having cystic fibrosis.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Epidemiology
questions.text: Which measure is used to describe the occurrence of new cases of papillomavirus infection in college students?
questions.explanation: Incidence measures the occurrence of new cases of a disease in a population over a specified period.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Gastroenterology
questions.text: What is the usual first-line imaging test for suspected acute cholecystitis?
questions.explanation: Right upper quadrant ultrasound is the usual first-line imaging test for suspected acute cholecystitis because it can detect gallstones, gallbladder wall thickening, pericholecystic fluid, and a sonographic Murphy sign.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Ophthalmology
questions.text: A patient presents to primary care with a unilateral painful red eye and no obvious discharge. What should the doctor do next?
options:
Referral to ophthalmology emergency
department for assessment
questions.explanation: A unilateral painful red eye is a potentially sight-threatening presentation. Urgent ophthalmologic assessment is appropriate when serious causes such as keratitis, uveitis, or acute glaucoma are possible.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Occupational Medicine
questions.text: A general practitioner sustains a needlestick injury while cannulating a patient who injects drugs. What is the most appropriate immediate management among the options?
options:
Encourage bleeding from site needle of the
stick injury
questions.explanation: The source patient may carry blood-borne viruses, so urgent occupational exposure assessment is required to determine HIV post-exposure prophylaxis and other testing. Immediate wound washing is also essential but is not offered as an option.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Infectious Diseases
questions.text: Which antituberculosis drug requires visual monitoring because of potential optic toxicity?
questions.explanation: Ethambutol can cause optic neuritis and visual impairment, so baseline and follow-up visual assessment are important, especially with prolonged therapy.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Rheumatology
questions.text: What is the classic confirmatory test for giant cell arteritis?
questions.explanation: Temporal artery biopsy has traditionally been the definitive diagnostic test for giant cell arteritis, although vascular ultrasound is increasingly used in some settings.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Orthopedics
questions.text: A patient develops a finger deformity after trauma with inability to extend the finger. What is an appropriate initial treatment for a closed extensor tendon injury such as mallet finger?
questions.explanation: Traumatic inability to extend a finger may represent an extensor tendon injury such as mallet finger; uncomplicated injuries are commonly treated with appropriate splinting, depending on the exact lesion.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Hematology
questions.text: Which laboratory test is most appropriate as an initial test for suspected pernicious anemia?
questions.explanation: Pernicious anemia causes vitamin B12 deficiency due to intrinsic-factor-related malabsorption. Serum vitamin B12 is a key initial laboratory test, with additional testing such as anti-intrinsic factor antibodies when needed.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Nutrition
questions.text: Which nutritional deficiency can cause gingival bleeding and hypertrophy?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy, characterized by impaired collagen synthesis, gingival disease and bleeding, bruising, and poor wound healing.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.text: A mother with significant hearing loss wants to confirm whether her newborn is deaf. Which objective hearing test should be used?
questions.explanation: Auditory brainstem response testing provides an objective assessment of auditory pathway function and is used for newborn hearing assessment, particularly when risk factors are present.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Neurology
questions.text: After carotid artery surgery, a patient has difficulty speaking and the tongue deviates to the right on protrusion. Which nerve is affected?
questions.explanation: The tongue deviates toward the side of a lower motor neuron hypoglossal lesion because the intact genioglossus pushes the tongue toward the affected side.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Oncology
questions.text: A patient with metastatic middle esophageal cancer has dysphagia. What is the best palliative method among the options to improve swallowing?
questions.explanation: For advanced esophageal cancer with dysphagia, an expandable esophageal stent can provide rapid luminal palliation and improve swallowing.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Rheumatology
questions.text: Which marker is most useful among the options for indicating systemic lupus erythematosus activity, including lupus nephritis?
questions.explanation: Anti-double-stranded DNA antibody levels often correlate with SLE disease activity and are particularly useful in monitoring lupus nephritis together with complement levels and clinical findings.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.text: A girl develops mild fever and malaise followed by vesicular lesions on the hands and feet with oral ulcers. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Hand-foot-and-mouth disease classically causes oral ulcers with vesicular lesions on the hands and feet and is commonly caused by Coxsackievirus, especially A16.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Respiratory Medicine
questions.text: An immunocompromised 62-year-old man has productive cough, dyspnea, and a chest X-ray showing infection. For which condition is sputum examination particularly indicated?
questions.explanation: In an immunocompromised patient with a respiratory infection, sputum testing is particularly important when pulmonary tuberculosis is suspected, especially for microbiologic confirmation and infection control.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Urology
questions.text: A 22-year-old man has a fluctuant scrotal swelling that cannot be separated from the testis and transilluminates brightly. What is the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: A hydrocele is a fluid collection around the testis that typically transilluminates brightly. It is usually fluctuant and may obscure palpation of the testis.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Gastroenterology
questions.text: Which investigation or marker is classically associated with hepatocellular carcinoma among the options?
questions.explanation: Alpha-fetoprotein is a classic serum tumor marker associated with hepatocellular carcinoma, although modern diagnosis relies heavily on liver imaging and AFP is not sufficiently sensitive to diagnose HCC alone.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Allergy
questions.text: Which form of urticaria-related swelling is most dangerous because of potential airway compromise?
questions.explanation: Angioedema can involve deeper tissues of the lips, tongue, pharynx, or larynx and may threaten the airway, making it the most dangerous option listed.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.text: A 3-year-old child weighs 12.5 kg and is prescribed a dose of 2 mg/kg of a suspension containing 50 mg in 5 mL. What volume is required per dose?
questions.explanation: Using the dose stated in the question: 2 mg/kg × 12.5 kg = 25 mg per dose. With 50 mg in 5 mL (10 mg/mL), 25 mg corresponds to 2.5 mL.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.text: A child is diagnosed with impetigo. What is the minimum commonly recommended period of school exclusion after starting appropriate treatment?
questions.explanation: Traditional school-exclusion guidance commonly allows return after at least 48 hours of appropriate antibiotic treatment and when lesions can be covered where applicable.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Cardiology
questions.text: A patient with hypertension has exertional chest pain. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Exertional chest pain in a patient with cardiovascular risk factors is typical of myocardial ischemia (stable angina), although the question is incomplete because options C and D are blank.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: With which drug should grapefruit be avoided because it can significantly increase drug exposure?
questions.explanation: Grapefruit juice inhibits intestinal CYP3A4 and can substantially increase simvastatin exposure, raising the risk of statin-associated myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.text: What is the most common causative organism of erysipelas?
questions.explanation: Erysipelas is classically caused by beta-hemolytic streptococci, especially group A Streptococcus.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Musculoskeletal
questions.text: Which analgesic can be used for a patient with back pain?
questions.explanation: The question is too nonspecific to identify one universally best drug. Acetaminophen can be used for pain, while NSAIDs such as ibuprofen or indomethacin may also be appropriate in selected patients if there are no contraindications.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Epidemiology
questions.text: Which study design is most appropriate for measuring the incidence of deep venous thrombosis?
questions.explanation: A cohort study can directly measure incidence because participants who are initially free of the outcome can be followed over time for new cases.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.text: Which of the following is an exogenous dermatitis?
questions.explanation: Irritant contact dermatitis is caused by external environmental or chemical exposure and is therefore an exogenous dermatitis.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.text: A patient has Trichophyton infection of the toenails. Which drug is generally preferred?
questions.explanation: Oral terbinafine is generally first-line therapy for dermatophyte onychomycosis because of its strong activity against dermatophytes such as Trichophyton.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: A patient is preparing for a CT scan with iodinated contrast. Which drug traditionally requires consideration of temporary withholding around contrast administration?
questions.explanation: The historical exam answer is metformin. Current guidance is more nuanced: metformin is not necessarily stopped for every iodinated contrast study, and withholding depends on kidney function and the clinical context.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.text: A child develops a rash and petechiae with pallor and hepatosplenomegaly. What is the next step?
options: Urgently send to a pediatric assessment unit

Give prednisolone for 3 days and them come
back

Give penicillin and send her by ambulance to
the hospital
questions.explanation: Pallor, petechiae, rash, and hepatosplenomegaly are red flags for serious hematologic disease such as leukemia and require urgent pediatric assessment rather than outpatient observation.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.text: A mother has a 2-day-old newborn and a 2-year-old child with chickenpox and is immune to varicella. What is the appropriate next step for the newborn based on the timing and nature of maternal infection and exposure?
options: Check the antibodies in the neonate
questions.explanation: The question is incomplete because management depends on the timing and nature of maternal infection, maternal immunity, and the newborn's exposure. The provided options do not include the key prophylaxis option of varicella-zoster immune globulin when indicated.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام صنعاء تاريخ 26/12/2024

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which of the following side effect of the thiazide drug
questions.explanation: Thiazide diuretics increase renal calcium reabsorption and can cause hypercalcemia. They more commonly cause hypokalemia, not hyperkalemia.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام عدن 2024 30/12/

questions.subject: Gastroenterology
questions.text: What is an appropriate eradication regimen for Helicobacter pylori?
questions.explanation: The listed combinations are incomplete H. pylori eradication regimens. Effective therapy requires a PPI plus appropriate antibiotics, with bismuth-containing quadruple therapy being a standard option.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام عدن 2024 30/12/

questions.subject: Respiratory Medicine
questions.text: What is the initial treatment of an acute asthma exacerbation?
questions.explanation: A short-acting inhaled beta2-agonist is a key first-line treatment for acute asthma exacerbation. Oxygen is added when hypoxemia is present.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام عدن 2024 30/12/

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which adverse effects are associated with ACE inhibitors?
questions.explanation: Both angioedema and hyperkalemia are recognized adverse effects of ACE inhibitors. However, cough is generally the most common characteristic adverse effect; therefore the wording 'most common side effect' is imprecise.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام عدن 2024 30/12/

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.text: Which imaging test is preferred for suspected acute appendicitis in a nonpregnant adult?
questions.explanation: In nonpregnant adults, CT abdomen/pelvis is generally the most accurate imaging test when imaging is required. Ultrasound is preferred initially in many children and during pregnancy.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام عدن 2024 30/12/

questions.subject: Neurology
questions.text: First Drug of choice in case of tonic-clonic seizure
questions.explanation: For an ongoing generalized convulsive seizure or status epilepticus, a benzodiazepine is first-line acute therapy. Phenytoin/fosphenytoin or valproate may follow when seizures persist.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام عدن 2024 30/12/

questions.subject: Neurology
questions.text: Which causes Wernicke encephalopathy.
questions.explanation: Wernicke encephalopathy results from thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency, classically in malnutrition or alcohol-use disorder.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام عدن 2024 30/12/

questions.subject: Neurology
questions.text: What does a positive Hoffmann sign suggest?
questions.explanation: The Hoffmann sign is an upper motor neuron sign suggesting corticospinal tract dysfunction; it is not a sign of DVT or peripheral arterial disease.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام عدن 2024 30/12/

questions.subject: Cardiology
questions.text: Which of the following is a recognized cause of secondary hypertension?
questions.explanation: Among the listed options, renal artery stenosis is a recognized cause of secondary hypertension. The most common overall secondary cause is often primary aldosteronism, depending on the population and definition.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام عدن 2024 30/12/

questions.subject: Endocrinology
questions.text: Most common cause of hypercalcemia in hospital
questions.explanation: In hospitalized patients, malignancy is a leading and classically the most common cause of hypercalcemia; primary hyperparathyroidism is more common in outpatient settings.
questions.source: نماذج مزاولة المهنة بكالوريوس طب عام عدن 2024 30/12/

questions.subject: Emergency Medicine
questions.text: Most common cause of air way obstruction in adult

questions.subject: Oncology
questions.text: Which is the risk factor for colorectal cancer

questions.subject: Infectious Diseases
questions.text: Treatment for meningitis

questions.subject: Respiratory Medicine
questions.text: Diagnostic test for Pulmonary embolism
questions.explanation: CT pulmonary angiography is the usual first-line definitive imaging test for many stable patients with suspected pulmonary embolism. V/Q scanning is an alternative when CT contrast or radiation considerations favor it.

questions.subject: Rheumatology
questions.text: Which drug of choice in acute gout flare
questions.explanation: Colchicine is an appropriate treatment for an acute gout flare. NSAIDs or corticosteroids are other first-line options. Allopurinol is for long-term urate lowering and should not be used as the acute anti-inflammatory treatment.

questions.text: About gall stones, all are true except.
options: Any patient with gall stones should have cholecystectomy.

questions.subject: Human Protozoal Diseases
questions.text: all are protozoa except:
questions.explanation: Filarial organisms are nematode helminths, not protozoa. Amoeba, Giardia and Toxoplasma are protozoan organisms.

questions.subject: Cyanosis at Birth
questions.text: A neonate at the delivery room has acrocyanosis, which is correct:
questions.explanation: Peripheral acrocyanosis can be a normal transitional finding in a newborn. Initial management includes maintaining warmth and assessing the newborn; oxygen is not automatically required for isolated acrocyanosis.

questions.subject: Brucellosis
questions.text: 12 years old child, live in rural area complaining of progressive fever, headache, arthralgia, by exam he has splenomegaly and hepatomegaly, what is the most probable diagnosis:
questions.explanation: A rural exposure with prolonged fever, arthralgia and hepatosplenomegaly is compatible with brucellosis, particularly in endemic settings and with animal or unpasteurized dairy exposure.

questions.subject: Peripheral Edema
questions.text: 55 years old male complaining of bilateral lower limb swelling, JVP normal, cardiac and respiratory auscultation was normal, no sign of CLD, what is the next step in investigation for abdomen
questions.explanation: With bilateral edema and no clinical evidence of heart failure or chronic liver disease, renal disease and proteinuria should be assessed; urinalysis is a basic next investigation.

questions.subject: Acute Epiglottitis
questions.text: A child with suspected acute epiglottitis should receive immediate controlled airway management, with intubation in a controlled setting by an experienced airway team when indicated.
options: immediate laryngoscopy in the operative room
questions.explanation: The presentation is classic for acute epiglottitis with impending upper-airway obstruction. The priority is securing the airway in a controlled environment; unnecessary throat examination or agitation should be avoided. Lateral neck radiography and CBC should not delay airway management.

questions.subject: Factor Xa and Thrombin Inhibition
questions.text: which of the following anticoagulant act factor Xa and on thrombin:
questions.explanation: Dalteparin is a low-molecular-weight heparin that potentiates antithrombin and inhibits factor Xa predominantly, with some anti-IIa (thrombin) activity. Apixaban selectively inhibits factor Xa, while dabigatran directly inhibits thrombin.

questions.subject: Cervical Cancer
questions.text: Pap smear for early detection of cervical cancer is:
questions.explanation: Screening detects disease or precancerous lesions early, which is secondary prevention. Primary prevention aims to prevent disease occurrence, such as HPV vaccination.

questions.subject: Pseudomonas Respiratory Infection
questions.text: 12 yrs old child, known case of cystic fibrosis complaining of chest infection due to pseudomonas, the drug of choice is:
questions.explanation: Ceftazidime has antipseudomonal activity and is a recognized option for Pseudomonas respiratory infection in cystic fibrosis. The source contains two unreadable/incomplete options.

questions.subject: Cervical Insufficiency
questions.text: about cerclage :
options: used as practical for any patient with history of pregnancy loss
questions.explanation: Cervical cerclage is commonly placed through a transvaginal approach. It is not indicated for every patient with a history of pregnancy loss, and routine removal does not necessarily require anesthesia.

questions.subject: Avascular Necrosis
questions.text: causes of avascular Necrosis, except:
questions.explanation: Common associations include sickle cell disease, dysbaric illness (caisson disease), corticosteroid exposure, alcohol excess and trauma. Chronic liver disease itself is not a standard primary cause of avascular necrosis.

questions.subject: Atrial Fibrillation
questions.text: 56 yrs old female, hypertensive, complaining of sudden episodes of palpitation, irregular, and associated with dizziness,
questions.explanation: Irregular palpitations in an older hypertensive patient are most consistent with atrial fibrillation among the listed choices.

questions.subject: Hyperglycemic Crisis
questions.text: In a patient with severe hyperglycemia, hypotension is most likely due to osmotic diuresis causing marked intravascular volume depletion.
questions.explanation: Hyperglycemic crises cause osmotic diuresis, dehydration and reduced circulating volume. The measured sodium of 123 mmol/L does not indicate hypernatremia; hyperglycemia can produce dilutional/translocational hyponatremia.

questions.subject: Perforated Appendicitis
questions.text: child with history of right lower quadrant pain, and diagnosed as perforated appendix, the organism that commonly cause sepsis peritonitis in this case are:
questions.explanation: Perforated appendicitis causes polymicrobial intra-abdominal infection, commonly involving Enterobacterales such as E. coli and anaerobes such as Bacteroides.

questions.subject: Vulvovaginal Candidiasis
questions.text: Female pt complaining of itching of vagina and cold like white discharge & redness of the vestibule : the diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Pruritus, vulvar erythema and thick white discharge are typical of vulvovaginal candidiasis.

questions.subject: Sanitation
questions.text: In a poor community with episodes of diarrhea, what is the simple way to limit diarrhea in this community:
questions.explanation: Improving sanitation and hygiene is a broad, sustainable community intervention that reduces diarrheal disease transmission.

questions.subject: Botulism
questions.text: Botulism occur in:
questions.explanation: Honey is a recognized source of Clostridium botulinum spores and should be avoided in infants younger than 12 months.

questions.subject: Vitamin A Deficiency
questions.text: child with night blindness, treated by:
questions.explanation: Night blindness is a classic manifestation of vitamin A deficiency. Cod liver oil contains vitamin A, although modern treatment should use an appropriate vitamin A preparation according to age and clinical context.

questions.subject: Pancreatitis
questions.text: Regarding pancreatitis which is true:
options: testing elastase in plasma not useful
questions.explanation: Serum lipase is more specific than amylase for acute pancreatitis and remains elevated longer. Urinary amylase and plasma elastase are not the standard first-line diagnostic tests.

questions.subject: Pancreatic Exocrine Insufficiency
questions.text: patient with chronic pancreatitis, has steatorrhea the cause of it is deficiency of what enzyme:
questions.explanation: Pancreatic lipase deficiency impairs fat digestion and causes steatorrhea in pancreatic exocrine insufficiency.

questions.subject: Major Burn Complications
questions.text: patient with ≥50% BSA, which is not the:
questions.explanation: Major burns cause immunosuppression, hypermetabolic hyperglycemia and can cause ARDS. The immediate systemic problem is usually hypovolemia from capillary leak and fluid loss, not hypervolemia.

questions.subject: Menstrual Cycle Disturbance
questions.text: Which of the following is least likely to cause menstrual cycle disturbance?
questions.explanation: Thyroid disorders are well-established causes of menstrual irregularity. Diabetes can also be associated with menstrual dysfunction, particularly when poorly controlled. PID is not a primary endocrine cause, but the question as written does not support a robust single answer.

questions.subject: Complications of Multiple Gestation
questions.text: Which of the following is NOT increased in multiple pregnancy? (No single valid answer among the visible options.)
questions.explanation: Multiple gestation increases risks of hypertensive disorders, gestational diabetes, placenta previa and fetal malpresentation. The visible options do not provide a clear exception.

questions.subject: Late-Onset HAP
questions.text: patient develop late onset hospital acquired pneumonia, what is the cause:
questions.explanation: Late-onset hospital-acquired pneumonia is commonly caused by resistant gram-negative bacilli and Staphylococcus aureus; Klebsiella is a plausible gram-negative pathogen, although the most common pathogen varies by setting.

questions.subject: Hip Instability
questions.text: Barlow test used to diagnose:
questions.explanation: The Barlow maneuver assesses whether an unstable neonatal hip can be displaced posteriorly, supporting detection of developmental dysplasia/hip instability.

questions.subject: Perinatal Hepatitis B Transmission
questions.text: Most common viral transmitted from mother to fetus is:
questions.explanation: Among the listed hepatitis viruses, hepatitis B is classically transmitted perinatally from mother to infant and is a major target of birth-dose vaccination and maternal screening.

questions.explanation: An uncomplicated cephalohematoma is managed conservatively with observation. It usually resolves spontaneously; aspiration or incision is avoided because of infection risk.

questions.text: The most common cause of vesicovaginal fistula in Yemen is:
questions.explanation: In low-resource settings, prolonged obstructed labor and obstetric trauma are major causes of vesicovaginal fistula.

questions.subject: Gastroenterology
questions.text: The most common gastrointestinal disorder in the community is:
questions.explanation: IBS is a common functional gastrointestinal disorder in the community.

questions.subject: Gastroenterology
questions.text: Which drug is NOT used in eradication of H. pylori?
questions.explanation: Cefixime is not a standard component of conventional H. pylori eradication regimens.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.text: Which drug does NOT cross the placenta?
questions.explanation: Unfractionated and low-molecular-weight heparins do not cross the placenta to a clinically significant extent.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.text: Regarding twin pregnancy, which is TRUE?
questions.explanation: Twin pregnancy increases the risk of postpartum hemorrhage, including from uterine overdistension.

questions.subject: Gynecology
questions.text: The most common cause of death in carcinoma of cervix is:
questions.explanation: Advanced cervical cancer can cause obstructive uropathy and renal failure, historically described as uremia.

questions.subject: Gastroenterology
questions.text: The most common cause of portal hypertension is:
questions.explanation: Cirrhosis is the most common overall cause of portal hypertension in many populations.

questions.subject: Hepatology
questions.text: The most common cause of fulminant hepatic failure is:
questions.explanation: Acute viral hepatitis is a recognized major cause of fulminant hepatic failure, particularly in regions where viral hepatitis is prevalent.

questions.subject: Nephrology
questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a criterion for nephrotic syndrome?
questions.explanation: Hypertension is not a defining criterion of nephrotic syndrome; massive proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia/edema and hyperlipidemia are characteristic.

questions.subject: Nephrology
questions.text: A recognized feature of minimal change disease is:
questions.explanation: Minimal change disease typically responds dramatically to corticosteroids, especially in children.

questions.subject: Gastroenterology
questions.text: The most common organism causing cholangitis is:
questions.explanation: Enteric Gram-negative organisms, especially E. coli, are common causes of acute bacterial cholangitis.

questions.subject: Nephrology
questions.text: All are complications of chronic pyelonephritis EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Chronic pyelonephritis is associated with scarring, hypertension and chronic renal impairment; septicemia is not a characteristic chronic complication.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.text: The surest sign of strangulated hernia is:
questions.explanation: A tense, tender, irreducible swelling strongly suggests compromised bowel and strangulation.

questions.subject: Neurology
questions.text: The most common cause of cerebrovascular accident (CVA) is:
questions.explanation: Cerebral thrombosis is a classic major cause of ischemic stroke, although modern classification includes several mechanisms.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.text: A risk factor for preeclampsia is:
questions.explanation: Pre-existing renal disease increases maternal risk of preeclampsia.

questions.subject: Gynecology
questions.text: Screening is most effective for:
questions.explanation: Cervical cancer has effective population screening programs using cervical cytology and/or HPV testing.

questions.subject: Gynecology
questions.text: A 65-year-old woman with postmenopausal bleeding. The most appropriate next step is:
questions.explanation: Postmenopausal bleeding requires endometrial assessment to exclude malignancy; the historical exam answer is tissue diagnosis by curettage/histopathology.

questions.subject: Infectious Diseases
questions.text: Protozoal infection transmitted by cats and undercooked meat is:
questions.explanation: Toxoplasma gondii is associated with cat feces and ingestion of undercooked infected meat.

questions.subject: Vascular Surgery
questions.text: Indication for amputation in chronic limb ischemia:
questions.explanation: Established irreversible tissue/neurologic loss may require amputation; isolated claudication is not an indication.

questions.subject: Urology
questions.text: A boy falls from a bicycle and has blood at the urethral meatus. Initial management:
questions.explanation: Blood at the urethral meatus suggests urethral injury; urinary diversion may be required, classically by suprapubic catheter when urethral catheterization is contraindicated.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.text: Which condition commonly requires surgery during pregnancy and carries an increased risk of preterm labor?
questions.explanation: Acute appendicitis is the commonest non-obstetric surgical emergency in pregnancy and surgery can increase preterm labor risk.

questions.subject: Urology
questions.text: A hemodynamically stable patient with blunt renal trauma has a renal laceration without urinary extravasation. Management is:
questions.explanation: Hemodynamically stable renal trauma without ongoing urinary extravasation is generally managed non-operatively with observation.

questions.subject: Gastroenterology
questions.text: A patient has obstructive jaundice due to a CBD stone with normal INR. The next step is:
questions.explanation: ERCP provides biliary decompression and stone extraction in appropriate patients with obstructing CBD stones.

questions.subject: Vascular Surgery
questions.text: Which is an indication for immediate vascular exploration after limb trauma?
questions.explanation: An absent distal pulse after limb trauma is a hard sign of arterial injury requiring urgent vascular assessment and often exploration.

questions.subject: Orthopedics
questions.text: The most important initial management of an open fracture is:
questions.explanation: Open fractures require urgent antibiotics, sterile coverage and surgical irrigation/debridement; among the listed choices, irrigation and debridement is the key intervention.

questions.subject: Trauma Surgery
questions.text: A patient has a knife injury with profuse bleeding. The best initial management is:
questions.explanation: Direct pressure is the first-line method for controlling most external hemorrhage; tourniquets are used when indicated for life-threatening extremity bleeding.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.text: A child has severe hip pain, fever (39°C), tenderness, and a normal X-ray. The diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Fever, focal bone/joint-region tenderness and severe pain with a potentially normal early radiograph are compatible with acute hematogenous osteomyelitis.

questions.subject: Gastroenterology
questions.text: A patient has progressive dysphagia to solids and barium swallow shows shouldering with irregular margins. Next step:
questions.explanation: Progressive solid-food dysphagia with shouldering and irregular margins suggests malignancy; endoscopy with biopsy establishes the diagnosis.

questions.subject: Gynecology
questions.text: The most common cause of vaginitis during pregnancy is:
questions.explanation: Vulvovaginal candidiasis is common during pregnancy because of hormonal and microbiologic changes.

questions.subject: Breast Surgery
questions.text: The most common site of breast cancer is:
questions.explanation: The upper outer quadrant is the most common site of breast cancer, partly because it contains a large volume of breast tissue.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.text: A patient develops respiratory distress due to neck hematoma after thyroidectomy. Immediate management is:
options: Open the wound immediately at the bedside
questions.explanation: Expanding neck hematoma with airway compromise is a surgical airway emergency; the wound should be opened immediately if needed to relieve compression.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of laparoscopic surgery?
questions.explanation: Longer operative time is a disadvantage rather than an advantage of laparoscopic surgery.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.text: A woman with a previous cesarean section is in labor on oxytocin. The most dangerous complication is:
questions.explanation: A scarred uterus exposed to labor and oxytocin carries a risk of uterine rupture, a potentially catastrophic complication.

questions.subject: Transfusion Medicine
questions.text: All are complications of blood transfusion EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Transfusion reactions more characteristically include allergic and hemolytic reactions; hypokalemia is not a typical transfusion complication.

questions.subject: Respiratory Medicine
questions.text: The most common presentation of pulmonary embolism is:
questions.explanation: Dyspnea is the most common presenting symptom of pulmonary embolism.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.text: Bleeding 10 days after hemorrhoidectomy is classified as:
questions.explanation: Secondary hemorrhage occurs later after surgery, often several days later, commonly from infection or sloughing of a vessel.

questions.subject: Trauma Surgery
questions.text: A trauma patient is unconscious with no evidence of cervical spine injury. The best initial definitive airway management is:
questions.explanation: In an unconscious trauma patient, airway protection and definitive airway management are prioritized. If there is no cervical spine injury concern, endotracheal intubation is generally preferred when a definitive airway is required.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.text: A woman develops sudden dyspnea and loss of consciousness after emergency cesarean section. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Sudden dyspnea and loss of consciousness after cesarean delivery are concerning for pulmonary embolism in a hypercoagulable postpartum patient.

questions.subject: Nephrology
questions.text: All of the following may cause red urine EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Microscopic hematuria does not visibly discolor urine red; myoglobinuria, hemoglobinuria and porphyria can cause red or dark urine.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.text: During pregnancy, the glomerular filtration rate (GFR) increases by:
questions.explanation: GFR rises substantially during pregnancy, commonly by approximately 40–50%.

questions.subject: Gastroenterology
questions.text: Antacids should be taken:
options: One hour after meals and at bedtime
questions.explanation: Traditional teaching recommends antacids after meals and at bedtime because gastric acid secretion and symptoms may increase postprandially and at night.

questions.subject: Respiratory Medicine
questions.text: Egg-shell calcification on chest X-ray is classically seen in:
questions.explanation: Peripheral 'egg-shell' calcification of hilar lymph nodes is classically associated with silicosis.

questions.subject: Neonatology
questions.text: The initial management of a vigorous newborn in the delivery room is:
options: Clear the airway by suctioning the mouth and nose if needed
questions.explanation: Routine newborn care begins with drying, warming, positioning and assessment of breathing and heart rate. Suctioning is not routinely performed unless the airway is obstructed.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.text: The most common cause of first-trimester abortion is:
questions.explanation: Chromosomal abnormalities account for a large proportion of early spontaneous miscarriages.

questions.subject: Oncology
questions.text: The best investigation for detecting bone metastasis is:
questions.explanation: Bone scintigraphy is a sensitive traditional whole-skeleton survey for many osteoblastic and mixed bone metastases.
